clue.text: Prize money, wife refused that being declared?

indicators.note: what is refused is turned away, so the wife's letter is not let in

blocks.note: money won as a prize
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone declaring their prize money to the taxman, after their wife refused to.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain may declare a team's innings closed, so the definition hides in tax-return language; cricket is a bat-and-ball game, and an innings is a team's turn at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket captain can end his side's batting turn early by declaring, so this is something that gets declared.

clue.text: Convict naval officer after case of insubordination

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so the first and last letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of insubordination
a mate is a ship's officer

explanation.surface: A sailor convicting an officer for insubordination.
explanation.walkthrough: Convict looks like a verb; it is the noun, a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict is a person serving a prison sentence, and an inmate is someone held in a jail.

clue.text: Small number having drink will purchase hot meal

indicators.note: to purchase is to acquire and take something in, so one letter is held inside the drink

blocks.note: NO is the abbreviated, small form of number
to sup is to drink
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A few people stopping for a drink before buying a hot meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot meal reads as the definition, but hot supplies a letter; nosh-up is British slang for a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is British slang for food, and a nosh-up is a large, satisfying meal.

clue.text: Casual midday half-hearted conversation across network

indicators.note: with half its heart gone, one of the two central letters is removed
lying across something means stretching over it, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: twelve o'clock noon
a chat is an informal conversation
a local area network

explanation.surface: A lazy lunchtime chat over a computer network.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonchalant means calmly unconcerned and relaxed, a synonym of casual in manner.

clue.text: Film captures European geese in flight

indicators.note: what captures something holds it inside, so the letter is enclosed

blocks.note: a film is a thin skin, as on milk
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A camera filming European geese flying overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Film looks like a movie; it is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is the collective term for a flock of wild geese flying in formation.

clue.text: Risk of sovereign giving up third of charities

indicators.note: third of points to one letter, the one in third position of the next word
giving up something means losing it, so a letter is surrendered from the longer word

blocks.note: belonging to an emperor or sovereign
the third letter of charities

explanation.surface: A worry that the monarch might stop donating to good causes.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil something is to put it in danger, so it is a verb synonym of risk.

clue.text: Senseless line in current record, one still unfinished

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so the line goes into the following letters
something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
I is the symbol for electric current
a log is a written record
Roman numeral one
calm means still, without wind

explanation.surface: A pointless line in a current record of a man still not finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The line sits inside current plus record taken together, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illogical lacks reason or coherence, which is what senseless means.

clue.text: Side each year, say, on the rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: PA, per annum, means each year
e.g. means for example, or say

explanation.surface: A team whose fortunes, year after year, are improving.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is one side of a sheet of paper in a book.

clue.text: Goes back on dustcart, Eric claims it's revolting

indicators.note: to claim is to take possession of, so the words hold the letters inside them
revolting can mean turning over, so the held letters are read backwards

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Eric insists the bin lorry is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting reads as disgusting, but it signals the reversal; a dustcart is a British rubbish truck.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a promise or statement is to withdraw it, which is what going back on means.

clue.text: Drop fine over incorrect method of rubbish disposal

blocks.note: to land is to come down, drop
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
as in ill-judged, wrong

explanation.surface: Dropping a fine for using the wrong way to get rid of waste.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' just puts one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Burying waste in a pit in the ground is a common way of getting rid of refuse, the site and process both called this.

clue.text: Graduate's working for stonecutter

blocks.note: MA, Master of Arts, a graduate, plus the 's
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A university graduate taking a job as a stonecutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who cuts and dresses building stone, a synonym for stonecutter.

clue.text: Teach lesson, it's said, on space

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the word before stands for one that sounds the same

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em wide
lesson sounds like lessen, and to lessen a load is to lighten it

explanation.surface: A teacher giving a lesson about outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: Across clues read 'A on B' as A after B, so the second piece follows the space. The homophone needs a second step: a synonym of the sound-alike word.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to give them knowledge or understanding, close to the verb teach.

clue.text: Hairy bird husband feeds dodged about regularly

indicators.note: to feed something is to put it inside, so the husband goes into the bird
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept
about can mean turned around, so the kept letters face the other way

blocks.note: a tropical bird with a huge bill
H is the abbreviation for husband
the second, fourth and sixth letters of dodged

explanation.surface: A shaggy bird with her husband gives someone the slip again.
explanation.walkthrough: Hairy is informal British for risky or frightening; the even letters of dodged are turned round and added after the bird with H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch and go describes a precarious situation whose outcome is uncertain, which is what hairy means as slang for perilous.

clue.text: Area above the ankle — and a little lower!

blocks.note: first meaning: the fleshy back of the lower leg
second meaning: a young creature that lows, that is, moos

explanation.surface: Pointing to a spot on the leg just above the ankle, then asking for a bit further down.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower here is not 'further down' but 'one that lows', a mooing animal; a little one is a baby cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the muscle at the back of the shin and the young of cattle, which low.

clue.text: Posh pal endlessly wrestling with scruples

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter goes
wrestlers twist and tangle, so the letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-to-do friend struggling with a guilty conscience.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh is informal for belonging to the highest social rank, the same as upper-class.

clue.text: Anarchy originally here the aim of London protesters?

definitions.text: Anarchy originally here the aim of London protesters?

blocks.clueFragment: Anarchy originally here the aim of London protesters?
blocks.note: surface reading: anarchists in London intend to bring the city to a standstill
setter's reading: the first letter of Anarchy in this clue is printed as an upper-case letter of the plain sort written on forms

explanation.surface: Anarchists in London hoping to halt the city with a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is also what demonstrators who want to stop traffic in London might be after: to block the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain upper-case letters, as used to fill in forms, are called this, and the A opening Anarchy is one.

clue.text: During election, hard to ignore division and timidity

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so one letter is dropped
during means within a period, so one word sits inside another

blocks.note: an election is a choice
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
a ward is an electoral division

explanation.surface: Candidates at an election shirking a vote out of fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of courage is cowardice, and timidity is a shy, fearful lack of nerve.

clue.text: Avoid eating large round slice of boneless meat

indicators.note: what eats takes something inside it, so letters go into the outer word

blocks.note: to escape is to avoid
L is the abbreviation for large
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Advice to skip a big round cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin slice of meat without bone, often veal, beaten flat and fried.

clue.text: Appreciative of good artist playing flute

indicators.note: playing about suggests movement, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
RA, Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A listener appreciating a skilled performer on the flute.
explanation.definitionFit: Grateful means thankful, feeling appreciation for something received.

clue.text: Stubborn requiring dwelling's rot to be treated

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A surveyor insisting that the decay in a house must be dealt with.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an unbending determination to have their way is obstinate, which is what stubborn means.

clue.text: Caribbean island boat almost got wrecked

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
something wrecked is broken up, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boat near a Caribbean island nearly ran aground and sank.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the smaller of the two main islands of Trinidad and Tobago, in the southern West Indies.

clue.text: Insist upon a banker being heard

indicators.note: being heard puts the sound first, so the phrase stands for a word pronounced the same

blocks.note: a banker is a sure thing, a cert

explanation.surface: Someone insisting that a bank worker be given a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker is betting slang for a certainty, and a cert is the British short form of certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state something forcefully, much as to insist does.

clue.text: Voice that's key source of opposition

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the Alt key on a computer keyboard
the first letter of opposition

explanation.surface: A voice that is the main origin of opposition, as in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singing voice, the lowest female or highest adult male range, so it names a type of voice.

clue.text: Extremely entertaining company, young but very mature

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one word is held inside another

blocks.note: as in precious little, meaning very little
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A youngster who is very good company and remarkably grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Extremely looks like the usual signal to take outer letters; it is a synonym, the adverb in phrases like 'precious few'.
explanation.definitionFit: A precocious child shows abilities or behaviour far beyond their age, so is young but advanced.

clue.text: Steal piano, overlooked by American Indian

blocks.note: the Cree are a Native American people
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A Native American stealing a piano unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, overlooked by puts the second piece below the first. Steal is the verb meaning move stealthily, not rob.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly and quietly to avoid notice, as to steal across a room.

clue.text: Group in supermarket turning up to grab bargain

indicators.note: grabbing takes hold, so the letters are held within the words
in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top, so the letters are backwards

blocks.note: letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A shopping group heading to a supermarket for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is British informal for something cheap, a real bargain.

clue.text: Rude attack

blocks.note: first meaning: insulting, causing affront
second meaning: a military assault or push

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a description of a crude assault; they are separate meanings, an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for insulting behaviour and also a noun for an army's forward campaign against an enemy.

clue.text: Saw band at intervals grow old

indicators.note: at intervals means with gaps between, so alternate letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of band
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Watching a band age over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw looks like the past of see or a tool; it is a noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old traditional saying, and an adage is a proverb of the same kind.

clue.text: Obscure online film excerpts attracting teens essentially

indicators.note: the essence of something is at its heart, so the central letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: E for electronic, as in e-mail
short extracts from a film
the middle letter of teens

explanation.surface: Obscure movie snippets on the internet pulling in a teenage audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to block it from view or outshine it, a verb synonym of obscure.

clue.text: Complete military training with a US post arranged

indicators.note: things arranged are put in a fresh order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A recruit finishing training and being sent to an American base.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadets pass out at a parade marking the end of their course, so the phrase means finishing military training.
